BEGIN WITH A PERSONAL ESSAY

What does a story owe the lives it touches?

A story can offer another way of seeing. I want to shape that invitation with care for the people represented and room for the person who reads.

FOLLOW A THREAD INTO LIFE

Three ways to keep reading.

Follow attention toward a first sentence, possibility into an imagined world, and a finished draft back into revision.

01 / ATTENTION & WITNESS

Before the first sentence

Attend to a life before turning it into a story.

  1. The same clearing. A different field of attention.

    Looking closely at one thing can make its surroundings harder to notice.

  2. What are they trying to do?

    Before answering, ask what the other person is trying to do.

  3. I trusted the process.

    A passage from Aaron’s own account.

02 / POSSIBILITY & WORLD

A world someone can enter

Follow possibility into a relationship with the reader.

  1. What can exist together?

    Some choices work together. Other combinations break a stated rule.

  2. Someone else can change the question.

    An outside reply can reveal a question we failed to ask ourselves.

  3. What changes when time is short?

    Waiting has different costs when needs are more urgent.

03 / REVISION & RESPONSIBILITY

The responsibility of revision

A finished sentence can still leave something important unheard.

  1. Let the correction leave a seam.

    When an explanation changes, leave a way to understand why.

  2. Remember to care.

    Who or what needs my attention here?

  3. What are they trying to do?

    Before answering, ask what the other person is trying to do.

The wider corpus remains open.

These are editorial connections. The readings retain their sources, disagreements and limits.
